lead.title: Apple's Claris previews 'Harbor', turning Apple silicon Macs into a private AI server with Thunderbolt 5 clustering
lead.summary: Claris, an Apple subsidiary, is privately previewing an app that turns Apple silicon Macs into private local-AI inference servers for open-weight models with no manual configuration. Harbor pools unified memory across multiple Macs over Thunderbolt 5 — accelerated by RDMA added in macOS Tahoe 26.2 — so a cluster can run models larger than any single Mac can hold.

top_stories.title: BotPsy: a 0.8B Apache-2.0 agentic model that doubles its base model's tool-use scores
top_stories.summary: Tether AI's BotPsy, built on Qwen3.5-0.8B, claims state-of-the-art function calling among models up to 1.2B parameters — BFCL v4 jumps from 23.4 to 44.0 and reasoning-loop stalls drop from 22.9% to 1.4%. Weights ship in bf16/Q8/Q4 as safetensors and GGUF for llama.cpp.

top_stories.title: Nod: n8n Labs ships a standalone open-source personal agent that runs on your computer
top_stories.summary: Nod is a research-preview desktop agent with its own computer and browser, separate from n8n itself. It is Apache 2.0, runs locally on macOS 14+/Windows 11 or your own server, and supports bring-your-own-model via OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter or a ChatGPT plan.

top_stories.title: llama.cpp b12274 adds FP8 KV-cache support for long-context inference
top_stories.summary: The release brings scaled FP8 KV-cache storage and dequantization (with Gemma 4 Assistant enabled for FP8 out of the box), cutting memory use for long contexts; b12271–b12282 also add backend scheduler reuse and chat fixes.

top_stories.title: GIGABYTE launches AI TOP AERO, an RTX Spark desktop with up to 128GB unified memory
top_stories.summary: The compact 'Personal AI Studio' box pairs NVIDIA's RTX Spark N1X Superchip (20-core Grace + Blackwell RTX) with up to 128GB LPDDR5x unified memory and a 4TB Gen5 SSD, targeting local development and inference with CUDA, LM Studio, Ollama and NVIDIA PAIR support.

items.title: Mobile AI Factory: an agent that builds task- and phone-specific small models
items.summary: An agentic system automatically searches base models, quantizations and inference engines with real on-device measurements; its on-device SLMs beat two five-shot frontier models on five of ten tasks across four Android phones, using 19x less GPU time than training all 27 variants.

items.title: HandsOnAid: a 4-bit offline first-aid assistant built for no-connectivity emergencies
items.summary: A quantized Gemma 2B fine-tuned with QLoRA on 5,550 FirstAidQA examples runs fully offline on a phone, with safety and accuracy evaluation aimed at emergency response.

items.title: SteerDistill: recovering agent task success after low-bit quantization
items.summary: Analysis of failed rollouts shows quantized agents overlook task requirements and drift from full-precision trajectories; closed-loop teacher steering recovers agent success under low-bit quantization.

items.title: Placing DeepSeek-V4.1's 203GB Engram lookup tables in host DRAM
items.summary: The Engram n-gram tables consume 190 of 223 GiB in a 4-GPU serving process; because row indices depend only on input tokens, reads can overlap earlier layers, so per-layer prefetch deadlines (differing 30x between two Engram layers) schedule placement in host memory.

items.title: MiniMax open-sources H3-Image: a 33B diffusion model generating natively at 4K
items.summary: One ~33.1B-parameter diffusion Transformer set (~68.65 GB of weights) handles both text-to-image generation and editing, accepts up to 16 reference images and generates directly at ~16 megapixels. Weights are on Hugging Face under a community license; the 'strongest instruction-following among open-source models' claim is vendor-stated.

items.title: KVARK Sparkle 1.1 (27B): Apache-2.0 document Q&A model that knows when to abstain
items.summary: The 27B model signals when an answer is not present in the source instead of hallucinating — a practical fit for local RAG pipelines where abstention matters more than raw generation quality.

items.title: Unsloth ships Dynamic v3.1 GGUF quants of Qwen3.8-27B
items.summary: The Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF repo updated with quants built using Unsloth's Dynamic v3.1 method — one of the most-downloaded current dense 27B checkpoints for llama.cpp, Ollama and LM Studio.

items.title: Tailscale OAuth apps go GA: agents reach private MCP servers on your tailnet
items.summary: Agents can now provision tailnet devices under a user's own identity instead of shared service tokens; Grok Bot already uses the flow to reach private MCP servers without exposing them to the public internet, with posture checks scoping access to just MCP servers.

items.title: Adobe releases a local MCP server exposing Creative Cloud to outside chatbots
items.summary: Announced at MAX, the server lets third-party chatbots such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini drive Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere and After Effects on native project files; the MCP release reaches Creative Cloud customers in early 2027.

items.title: Warmctl: fast cold starts for vLLM inference
items.summary: TensorRails' open-source tool attacks vLLM cold-start latency, a common pain point for self-hosted inference serving.

items.title: Ollama v0.40.17-rc0: mmap for Vulkan integrated GPUs, concurrent MLX generation
items.summary: The pre-release adds mmap support for Vulkan integrated GPUs, concurrent generation in the MLX runner and a llama.cpp bump to b12257 — following v0.40.16, which cut Qwen3.8 Flash Next memory use by ~27 GiB on Apple silicon.

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon now available in n8n for agent workflows
items.summary: n8n added support for Google's Gemini 4 Carbon (53.9% on AutomationBench), recommending it for heavy-reasoning agent steps while keeping lighter models for classification and formatting — including on self-hosted instances via your own API key.

items.title: What breaks when a self-hosted LLM gateway hits 1,000 concurrent streams
items.summary: A practical engineering write-up on failure modes of self-hosted OpenAI-compatible gateways under ~1,000 concurrent streaming connections — connection limits, buffering behavior, and where llama.cpp/vLLM-style stacks degrade first.

items.title: Updated break-even math: self-hosted vs API for the four open-weight models worth hosting
items.summary: A November cost comparison of Kimi K3.1 Pro, GLM-5.3, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Mistral Large 4 against API pricing concludes Mistral Large 4 is the strongest self-host candidate on current hardware economics.

items.title: Team Group CEO warns the memory shortage peaks through Q2 2027: 'even money can't buy goods'
items.summary: DRAM/NAND shortage will be most severe from Q4 2026 through Q2 2027 with no price decline expected in 2027 and balance not before H2 2028, per the CEO; 16Gb DDR5 contract prices rose from $8.70 in October 2025 to $48 in September 2026 — a direct cost driver for RAM-heavy local rigs.

items.title: ExecuTorch adds an experimental WebGPU backend for PyTorch models in the browser
items.summary: Exported .pte models now run on the user's GPU inside WebGPU-enabled browsers, with reported 4-7x faster prefill and 2-10x faster decode versus the CPU path on quantized Llama 3.2 1B and Qwen3-0.6B — though the partitioner can still wrap operators WebGPU cannot execute.
